answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. So the design does not rely on catching every cheat — it makes cheating unprofitable, which is a far more stable defense than any whitelist ever could be. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost.
